newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds edge down amid sell-off of German bund.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds edge down amid sell-off of German bund.

text.p: Irish government bonds edged lower in thin late trade on Thursday in line with Germany amid good selling interest in German bunds, dealers said.
"There seems to be a bit of selling of German bunds going on and they have come back this afternoon, dampening talk of a repo cut," one dealer said.
Dealers said there had been hopes for a repo cut earlier after comments from Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp and a Bundesbank report predicting little threat from inflation.

Krupp's comments stimulated earlier gains, saying that he was worried about high German unemployment: "Even monetary policy cannot be indifferent to this situation, particularly when it does not need to have any worrries about inflation."

In its January monthly report, the Bundesbank said it expected inflation to stay below two percent for the next two years, with prices capped by unemployment, globalisation of markets and the general view that inflation is an evil.
By 1630 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had risen five pence from Wednesday's close at 102.40 to yield 5.90 percent having been at 102.50 earlier in the day.
The key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 had gained 20 pence at 109.85 to yield 6.46 percent having been at 109.90 earlier.
